Summary
: This is the Sanskrit edition Kavyalankara Sara Sangraha, including the Laghuvritti commentary of Induraja, an English introduction, notes and appendices. The “Kavyalamkara Sara Samgraha” by Udbhata is a significant work in the field of Sanskrit poetics, primarily focusing on poetic figures and rhetoric (alamkara). It dates back to the late 8th century and represents a crucial link between the earlier works of Bhamaha and the later refinement by Mammata, considered pivotal figures in the development of Alamkara literature. Udbhata's treatise, which includes commentary by Induraja, explores around 41 figures of speech, deriving major influences from Bhamaha while establishing its uniqueness with original contributions. 
The Kavyalankara Sara Sangraha underwent a challenging editorial process involving prominent scholars like Dr. Buhler and later, authorities from the Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute. This edition faced many delays and was finally published after being meticulously prepared from various manuscripts collected across India. The book also documents the familial and scholarly connections of figures like Induraja within the broader context of Kashmir's literary tradition. Udbhata's work plays a vital role in the historical trajectory of Indian rhetorical theory, illustrating the evolution and indigenous richness of Sanskrit literary aesthetics.
